title: Your own strings tool
description:
Write `findStrings(bytes, minLength)`, which scans a block of bytes for text the way the `strings` tool does, in both encodings:

- **ASCII**: a run of at least `minLength` printable bytes (0x20 to 0x7E inclusive).
- **UTF-16**: a run of at least `minLength` two-byte units, each a printable ASCII byte followed by a zero byte, starting at an **even** offset.

Return every string found, as an offset and the text (UTF-16 strings converted to their ASCII letters), sorted by offset. A UTF-16 string's bytes are not also reported as ASCII (its letters are separated by zeros, so they are never `minLength` long as ASCII anyway, for `minLength >= 2`).

```
bytes: 00 'H' 'P' ':' ' ' '9' '9' 01 'S' 00 'a' 00 'v' 00 'e' 00 00 00
minLength 4
-> { 1, "HP: 99" }  { 8, "Save" }
```
hints: Do two separate scans. The ASCII scan walks byte by byte, building a run of printable characters and recording it when a non-printable byte (or the end) arrives, if it is long enough.
The UTF-16 scan walks two bytes at a time from offset 0, so every unit starts at an even offset. A unit counts when its first byte is printable and its second is zero.
Sort the combined results by offset at the end: pairs sort by their first element.
